title: Nonconvex first-order stationarity with ordinary value-gradient and rich full-Hessian jets: joint fixed budgets
summary: Minimize the number of ordinary calls under a prescribed rich-call cap, retaining the native joint (G,H) resource. The randomized lower and deterministic upper match in the stated logarithmic-dimension, small-rich-budget window.

description_paragraphs: Find a point with gradient norm at most the prescribed tolerance for a globally Hessian-Lipschitz, possibly nonconvex objective.

model.parameter_domain_latex: d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1},\ \Delta\ge0,\ L_2>0,\ \varepsilon>0,\ h\in\mathbb N_0;\quad T=\Delta\sqrt{L_2}/\varepsilon^{3/2}
description_paragraphs: The unknown objective f:R^d->R is C^2, has a finite infimum, and obeys f(x_0)-inf f<=Delta at the public initial point x_0.
For every x,y in R^d, ||H_f(x)-H_f(y)||_op<=L_2||x-y||_2. There is no bound on ||H_f(x)||, no separate gradient-Lipschitz parameter, and no convexity assumption.
The normalized class is F_d(T)={u in C^2(R^d): inf u> -infinity, u(0)-inf u<=T, Lip(H_u)<=1}. Its target is ||grad u||<=1.

The Delta=0 endpoint is included by a local argument. A positive public L_2 may bound an instance whose actual Hessian Lipschitz constant is zero; the separate parameter case L_2=0 is not part of this profile.

hidden_objects.description: The objective, its unqueried jets, its minimum value and any minimizer are hidden.

description_paragraphs: At any point, choose an ordinary response containing the value and full gradient, or a rich response containing the value, full gradient and full Hessian.
One rich call increments H only. Its included value and gradient do not also increment G. An ordinary call increments G only. Full Hessians are returned, not Hessian-vector products.
Queries may be arbitrary exact-real vectors with arbitrarily small positive separations. No radius, span, periodic-access rule, sampling interface, or weighted price is imposed.

output.certificate: No additional certificate or queried-point restriction.
description_paragraphs: Return an arbitrary point in R^d. The output may be unqueried.
The target is the gradient norm itself; no squared-norm or expected-error conversion is implicit.

resource.unit_cost: Native integer vector (G,H): one ordinary response or one rich response, charged exclusively to its own counter.
free_operations: Exact real arithmetic, memory and linear algebra
Global solution of known finite-dimensional models
description_paragraphs: Both caps hold on every execution path, including unsuccessful runs. Initialization, repeated responses and all actual stopping checks are charged. Expected query counts are not substituted.
The principal scalar comparison minimizes the ordinary cap G subject to the prescribed rich cap H<=h. The native joint feasible region is retained as a second quantity.

Policies enforce caps even on counterfactual histories, terminating before an excess call. Internal work is uncharged but must terminate in finitely many measurable steps on every legal input; no uniform arithmetic-time bound is required.
A feasible pair must be witnessed by one algorithm. Coordinatewise upper bounds from unrelated algorithms are not combined into a joint pair.

views.label: Unrestricted randomized algorithms; per-instance success

internal_computation_restrictions: Finite measurable termination on each legal input
description_paragraphs: Arbitrary measurable adaptive policies may use a private random seed independent of the fixed input. Queries and outputs are unrestricted exact-real points.
Finite parameter-dependent advice is allowed when independent of the unknown instance. No span, Krylov or zero-respecting condition is imposed.
Every adopted upper witness is deterministic; every cited main lower bound applies to unrestricted randomized policies.

guarantees.uniformity: Choose one algorithm from the public parameters; require the probability guarantee separately for every fixed admissible instance.
description_paragraphs: Probability is over the algorithm seed after fixing the objective. There is no oracle noise. Deterministic witnesses succeed on every instance and therefore satisfy this view.

display_qualifications:
**Native accounting.** An ordinary response contains $(f,
abla f)$ and costs one $G$; a rich response contains $(f,
abla f,
abla^2f)$ and costs one $H$ only. Both budgets are fixed pathwise caps.

**Matching window.** With $T=\Delta\sqrt{L_2}/\varepsilon^{3/2}$, constant-factor matching is asserted for $T\ge T_0$, $d\ge C_{\rm dim}\log(2+T)$, $1\le h$ and $h+1\le aT$. The two branch rows partition this window. Other rows keep their own guards.

**Joint scope.** The joint row gives proved feasible pairs and conditional necessary inequalities. It does not identify the whole Pareto frontier, the sharp rich-only threshold, or all results in the literature.

quantities.label: Minimum ordinary cap under a prescribed rich cap
quantities.expression_latex: Q_g^\star(h;d,T)=\min\{g\in\mathbb N_0:\exists A,\ \forall f,\omega:\ G_A(f,\omega)\le g,\ H_A(f,\omega)\le h;\ \forall f:\Pr_\omega[\|\nabla f(\widehat x_A)\|\le\varepsilon]\ge2/3\}
quantities.definition_note: A single algorithm, chosen using only public inputs, must terminate on every legal instance and path. T is obtained by a one-response-for-one-response rescaling. Q_g counts ordinary calls only, excluding gradients included in rich calls.

quantities.label: Joint feasible ordinary/rich budget region
quantities.expression_latex: \mathcal B^\star(d,T)=\{(g,h)\in\mathbb N_0^2:\exists A\text{ satisfying main/g1 with }(G_A,H_A)\preceq(g,h)\text{ on every path}\}
quantities.definition_note: The set is upward closed. Its h-slice satisfies Q_g^star(h;d,T)=min{g:(g,h) in B^star}. Bounds below describe proved attainable families and conditional necessary constraints, not an exact global frontier.

proofs.title: Literal rich caps, upper-envelope extension, and additive-d absorption
proofs.statement: The generic upper and the two matching branches follow from the two explicitly translated NALEN implementations.
proof_steps: Proposition A.1(ii) gives H=0 and G<=C_0(d+T d^(1/3)) for T>=1; A.1(i) gives H<=h and G<=C_1 T^(3/2)/sqrt(h) for every integer 1<=h<=T.

For any T>=0 the normalized class with gap T is a subclass of the class with gap Tbar=max{1,T}. The pure-ordinary witness therefore gives the global ordinary upper. If h>=1, k=min{h,floor(Tbar)} is an integer in [1,Tbar], and the mixed witness obeys H<=k<=h. Selecting by public upper bounds yields U(h;d,T).
If T>=1, 1<=h<=T and d<=(T/h)^(3/2), then d^(2/3)<=T/h<=T and hence d<=T d^(1/3). The pure-ordinary upper is at most a constant times T d^(1/3).
If d>(T/h)^(3/2), the mixed upper is at most a constant times T^(3/2)/sqrt(h). Thus the minimum-form upper holds for all 1<=h<=T, without a lower-dimension requirement.

On the source lower window, h<=h+1<=2h. If A=T d^(1/3) and B=T^(3/2)/sqrt(h), then min{A,B/sqrt(1+1/h)}>=min{A,B}/sqrt(2). This matches both branches by absolute constants; no logarithm in d or h is discarded.

Strict cap detail from Appendix A: choose m=ceil(A_0(T/h)^(3/2)) and N=hm, with snapshots at 0,m,...,(h-1)m. The number of rich snapshots is at most h; ordinary initialization and stationarity tests are included in the bound <=3N+1. For the zero-rich version, symmetrized coordinate differences approximate each Hessian with d+1 ordinary queries; m=d gives total O(d+T d^(1/3)). The small finite-difference steps are legal because exact-real precision is uncharged.

proofs.statement: At h=0, the adopted lower is Omega(min{T d^(1/3),T^(3/2)}) when T>=T_0 and d>=C_dim log(2+T).
proof_steps: Any algorithm with rich cap zero is admissible under rich cap one with the same ordinary cap. Hence Q_g^star(0)>=Q_g^star(1).
Because T_0>=2/a, the source condition h+1<=aT holds at h=1. The other lower-theorem conditions are exactly the h0_lower regime. Substituting h=1 yields c_L min{T d^(1/3), T^(3/2)/sqrt(2)}.
For d<=T^(3/2), the ordinary upper has d<=T d^(1/3), and the lower is at least c_L T d^(1/3)/sqrt(2); this establishes a constant-factor bracket.

This consequence does not claim that the explicit h=0 parameter theorem has been fully optimized, or that these are all existing zero-rich results.

proofs.title: Zero-gap endpoint and an explicit rich-only sufficient cap
proofs.statement: Delta=0 allows no calls; for any Delta>0, G=0 and H<=floor(12T)+2 suffice.
proof_steps: If Delta=0 then the differentiable objective attains its global infimum at the public x_0. Its gradient is zero, so return x_0 with no response. Nonnegativity of caps proves exact ordinary complexity zero.

For Delta>0, at the current point request one rich jet (f,g,H). If ||g||<=epsilon, return. Otherwise select a global minimizer s of the known coercive cubic model m(s)=g^T s+(1/2)s^T Hs+(L_2/3)||s||^3, and move to x+s. A measurable global-minimizer choice is an allowed uncharged internal operation.
Hessian Lipschitz continuity gives f(x+s)<=f(x)+g^T s+(1/2)s^T Hs+(L_2/6)||s||^3. Since m(s)<=m(0)=0, f(x)-f(x+s)>=(L_2/6)||s||^3.
Model stationarity gives g+Hs+L_2||s||s=0. The gradient Taylor remainder has norm at most (L_2/2)||s||^2, so ||grad f(x+s)||<=(3L_2/2)||s||^2.

If the next point fails the target, then ||s||>(2epsilon/(3L_2))^(1/2); its objective decrease is greater than [(1/6)(2/3)^(3/2)]epsilon^(3/2)/sqrt(L_2) and hence greater than epsilon^(3/2)/(12sqrt(L_2)). There can be at most floor(12T) such failing next points.

One initial rich check and the final successful rich check therefore give H<=floor(12T)+2, while G=0 throughout. All intermediate checks are included. The gap bounds the number of iterations and the model solve is finite under the permitted abstract measurable-operation convention.

This explicit proof is supplied for the present contract. Nesterov-Polyak is a background reference for cubic regularization, not a claim that its theorem uses the displayed constant 12. No optimality is asserted for H_cub itself.

proofs.title: Direction-preserving transfer from cap slices to joint budgets
proofs.statement: The joint record retains attainable pairs and conditional necessary constraints without inventing a global Pareto curve.
proof_steps: The ordinary-only algorithm has a single fixed pair (ceil(C_0(d+Tbar d^(1/3))),0). For each integer j in [1,floor(Tbar)], the mixed algorithm has the single pair (ceil(C_1 Tbar^(3/2)/sqrt(j)),j). The cubic algorithm has (0,H_cub). At T=0 return x_0 for (0,0).

Increasing either cap preserves feasibility for the same algorithm, proving upward closure of these attainable pairs. Randomly mixing algorithms, taking convex hulls of budgets, or merging their separate coordinate minima is neither needed nor justified.

If one algorithm witnesses a feasible pair (G,H), then by definition G>=Q_g^star(H;d,T). Applying the main lower at this same H yields the joint conditional inequality when 1<=H and H+1<=aT. For H=0 use the separate monotonicity proof. Both require the displayed scale and dimension conditions.

No necessary constraint is inferred in a region where these premises are absent. Thus the paired record does not certify the full feasible region, the smallest zero-ordinary threshold, or an exact large-rich transition.
